memory_update.text: PLPC should be retained as the highest-priority underfollowed candidate for the transmission_hardware_fittings node because it is a narrow public manufacturer of formed wire and conductor-related hardware with direct grid and communications network exposure.

HUBB is a useful diversified reference competitor for transmission and substation hardware demand, but its exposure is diluted by broader utility, grid controls, meters, gas distribution, and electrical solutions businesses.

VMI is an adjacent chokepoint candidate for transmission structures, poles, substations, and coatings; include in later layers only if Utility segment backlog and margin evidence confirms grid-transmission leverage.
MYRG is not a hardware supplier, but it can serve as a smaller-cap installation/EPC read-through for hardware procurement timing, lineworker scarcity, and utility construction demand.

Private competitor MacLean Power Systems appears important for product-for-product comparison but is not directly investable as a standalone public company; later research should map PLPC/HUBB/MacLean product overlap and utility qualification barriers.

node: Transmission-line hardware, fittings, conductor accessories, and installation-enabling components
summary: Expanded the node around transmission-line hardware and installation-enabling components with a two-lane universe. The clearest underfollowed pure-play is Preformed Line Products, while Hubbell serves as a diversified reference competitor, Valmont as an adjacent transmission-structure supplier, and MYR Group as an installation/EPC read-through for labor-constrained grid buildout. The main underappreciated angle is that hardware procurement, utility qualification, and installation compatibility can create earlier demand signals than visible transmission construction revenue.
